citation.note: Written notice of pay decreases 1+ pay periods in advance, stating the old rate, new rate, and effective date; pay increases take effect immediately with no advance-notice duty (§ 40.1-29).

Salary-history ban (§ 40.1-28.7:12, effective 2026-09-03): employers cannot seek or require prior compensation; voluntarily disclosed history may only justify a higher offer; retaliation for refusal is barred.

body.context: setting compensation for a promotion or base-pay change

citation.note: Payroll records (name, address, occupation, hours, rate, gross/net pay, deductions) kept 3 years; 3-year wage-claim limitations period (§ 40.1-29).
Hourly workers paid at least biweekly (every 14 days) or semimonthly (§ 40.1-29).
Salaried workers paid at least monthly (§ 40.1-29).
Final pay on separation (§ 40.1-29): all earned wages on or before the next regular payday following separation; knowing violations face treble damages plus 8% annual interest (§ 40.1-29.2).

body.deadline_description: All earned wages on or before the next regular payday following separation; knowing violations face treble damages plus 8% annual interest (§§ 40.1-29, 40.1-29.2).

citation.note: Wage-range disclosure in all public and internal postings, in good faith from the pay scale or comparable roles, effective 2026-09-03; range disclosed on applicant request; retaliation barred; Attorney General penalties $1,000 first offense / $5,000 subsequent with a 1-year private action (§ 40.1-28.7:12).

body.required_disclosure: Wage/salary range in all public and internal postings, disclosed in good faith, effective 2026-09-03; range on applicant request; $1,000/$5,000 penalties with a 1-year private action (§ 40.1-28.7:12).

citation.note: Non-competes void for low-wage employees (threshold per § 65.2-500/BLS median), FLSA-overtime-eligible employees, and all healthcare professionals (SB 1218, effective 2025-07-01); unenforceable after without-cause termination without severance, compensation, or paid leave; $10,000 civil penalty with a 2-year employee action (§ 40.1-28.7:8).

body.rule: Void for low-wage, FLSA-overtime-eligible, and healthcare-professional employees (SB 1218, effective 2025-07-01); void after without-cause termination without severance or paid leave; $10,000 penalty, 2-year action (§ 40.1-28.7:8).

citation.note: Minimum wage floor check (§ 40.1-28.10): verify any new rate against the current state minimum - $12.77 (2026-2027), $13.75 (2027-2028), $15.00 (2028-2029), then annual CPI-U adjustment. No tip credit: tipped employees receive the full minimum.

Equal pay for equal work irrespective of sex (§ 40.1-28.6): flag promotion rates that differ from peer rates for equal skill, effort, responsibility, and similar working conditions; seniority, merit, production, or a factor other than sex justify a differential.

Pay statements show employer name and address, hours worked, rate of pay, gross and net wages, and the amount and purpose of each deduction, with enough detail to verify gross-to-net math; retained 3+ years (§ 40.1-29).

Contractor classification uses the common-law/IRS control test (control, payment method, tools, permanence, integral nature of the work); no ABC statutory test. Misclassification enforced by the Department of Labor, Department of Revenue, and Workers' Compensation Commission with back wages, reclassification, and civil actions (§ 40.1-28.7:7).

body.test_description: Common-law/IRS control test for contractor status; no ABC statutory test (§ 40.1-28.7:7).

citation.note: Current or former employees receive copies of retained records (dates of employment, wages, title and description, workplace injuries) within 30 days of a written request, for a reasonable copying fee; narrower than a full personnel-file law, and a written disagreement accompanies third-party disclosures (§ 8.01-413.1, effective 2019-07-01).

§ 40.1-28.7:9 (Wage Discussion Protection, 2022): Employer cannot discharge, discipline, threaten, discriminate against, or retaliate against employee for inquiring about, discussing, or disclosing own wages, other employees' wages, or filing a wage complaint with the Commissioner (including hours and pay information).

No state-level regulation of private-sector drug testing; federal law and DOT rules apply. Marijuana possession inquiry limits (§ 19.2-389.3) and medicinal-cannabis-oil discharge protection (§ 40.1-27.4) are hiring-inquiry rules, not testing rules.
